title: FACT CHECK: No Supreme Court arrest warrant for NBI director Matibag
summary: No such report has been released or published on the official website and communication channels of the Supreme Court

blocks.text: Claim: The Supreme Court (SC) has issued an arrest warrant against National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag.

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 584,000 views, 2,400 shares, and 1,500 comments as of writing. It was posted on November 7 and continues to gain traction up to this date.

The reel shows photos of Vice President Sara Duterte, Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte, Supreme Court Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, and Matibag. The text overlaid on the reel says, “Kulong na! Warrant nilabas ng korte kumpirmado na! Walang takas!”
(Off to jail! Court issues warrant. Confirmed! No escape!)
Some of the Facebook users in the comment section believed the claim that the SC issued a warrant and that Matibag is set to be jailed.

The facts: No such arrest warrant has been released or published on the official website and communication channels of the SC. Likewise, there are no official government statements or credible media reports indicating that a court has issued a ruling in a case involving Matibag that would have led to the issuance of a warrant. The Facebook reel also did not show any credible source to support its claim.
Contrary to the post’s claim, Matibag has not been jailed. He recently made a public appearance on November 13 during the NBI’s 90th anniversary celebration in Manila.
A reverse image search shows that a graphic shown in the Facebook reel came from a YouTube video by “PINAS BALITA TV,” a channel that posts content previously flagged by Rappler.

In this video, the commentator mentioned that the NBI filed a complaint against former Davao City chief information officer Jefry Tupas on October 26 over alleged obstruction of justice, cyber libel, and publication of false news.

The case stemmed from an affidavit by former police corporal Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., who claimed that Tupas received millions of pesos intended for the Vice President. Amid the NBI’s investigation, Tupas alleged that the bureau attempted to bring him to Manila and offered him security, money, and accommodation, citing supposed threats to his life.

While the NBI complaint is genuine, it is not true that Tupas in turn filed a complaint against the bureau. The SC is not involved in the NBI’s complaint against Tupas, either.Libel: On October 23, Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte filed cyber libel complaints against Matibag, Gracioso, and GMA Network journalists over the latter’s report about bribery claims against him and the Vice President.Gracioso, in an affidavit submitted to the NBI, alleged that he delivered millions of pesos to the Vice President when she was still the mayor of Davao City. GMA was the first to report about the affidavit.

In a November 10 letter obtained by GMA News, Paolo Duterte asked Matibag to inhibit himself from the investigation into Gracioso’s claims. The NBI director rejected the request, saying it had no legal basis.
No court ruling or arrest warrant has been issued related to the case.

blocks.text: Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.
